headline: South Korea's president ordered a full investigation after data leaks spread from major banks to savings banks and lenders in four days.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: confirmed by the presidential office and the regulator, and the attack wave is widening.
importance_line: Tens of thousands of bank customers now face phishing risk from leaked names, incomes and ID numbers, regulators have put the whole Korean financial sector on alert, and the banks must prove their defences; whether AI tools really drove the attacks is still only a suspicion.
summary: The Korea Times reports that President Lee Jae Myung on Sunday ordered a thorough investigation after Shinhan Bank's leak of about 25,000 customers' data on Thursday was followed within two days by leaks at KB Kookmin, Hana and BNK Busan banks, Yegaram Savings Bank (about 40,000 customers) and Hyundai Capital. New today: regulators called an emergency meeting of the entire sector, the Financial Services Commission chairman said AI-powered attacks "cannot be ruled out", and industry officials told the paper that traces of a Chinese-language AI penetration-testing tool were found on a server used against Shinhan.
notes: Follow-up of 3 Oct item C12-01 (Shinhan breach): new today is the presidential order, the sector-wide emergency meeting and the spread to non-bank lenders. Reuters version blocked; Korea Times own reporting used. Also reported by Korea JoongAng Daily.
